doc.title: Dave Brubeck — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Nixon's Ellington birthday night
summary: Nixon's speech that Duke's father had been a butler in the White House moved Brubeck.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: I see. What’s the protocol for that? Do you play a whole set? Do you play just one or two numbers?

You play maybe three or four. The Ellington night, there’s so many jazz musicians that you just go up and play one tune. When I think of the Ellington night, I think of the night that I really liked Dick Nixon, who I hadn’t been a fan of. But he said – we’re at the dinner in a separate room. He gets up to make a speech of welcome. He said, “In this room there’s been welcome and entertainment for kings and queens and leaders of the world, but tonight we entertain our first Duke.” Then he said, “It’s come full circle. Duke’s father was the head” – did he call him . . .

“. . . butler in this room. Tonight we’re entertaining and honoring his son.” Isn’t that great? It was so wonderful. Iola was sitting with Mercer [Ellington] in a room full of musicians and great statesmen. I don’t know why I got on that, but I was thinking of how great that was, Duke being raised in Washington.
That’s right. His father catered meals at the White House.
His father catered meals at the White House.
Yeah, and wasn’t it wonderful of Nixon to bring that . . .
